title: Find out whether Command Z works after clicking a control in the right hand panel
goal: After you click something in the right hand panel - a switch, a menu - pressing Command Z may do nothing at all, so the change you just made cannot be taken back with the keyboard. This is about finding out whether that is real for a person or only an artefact of the scripted walks, and fixing it if it is real.
notes:
Seen on 2026-09-12 while building the Blending row. Two walks, one on the NEW control and one on a control that predates this work, both fail the same way, so it is not a regression from the blend work.

Run 1, the new control:
  Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/undo-probe.json --no-build
  draw a rectangle, press Blending, press Multiply, expect Blending reads Multiply (passes), press Command Z, expect Normal
  -> step 13 (expect): the control called "Blending" reads "Blending, Multiply", not "Blending, Normal"

Run 2, the CONTROL experiment on an old control:
  Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/undo-control.json --no-build
  draw a rectangle, press the Fill switch (turning Fill off), press Command Z, expect Fill reads on
  -> step 10 (expect): the control called "Switch" reads "Fill, off", not "Fill, on"

In both the log says the key WAS delivered: [47 key] command+z taken by responder chain. So something in the chain claims it and does not undo, or the undo happens and the panel does not follow. An { "do": "action", "action": "undo" } step in the same place works every time, which is why blend-mode-walk.json uses that.

First thing to try is by hand in the probe: draw a box, click the Fill switch, press Command Z, look. If it undoes for a person then the walk harness sends the key to the wrong responder after a panel press and the fix is in PlaytestHarness, not in the app.
acceptance: A plain statement of whether a person pressing Command Z after clicking a panel control gets their change undone, backed by trying it in the app
If it is broken, Command Z undoes the last change after a panel control was clicked, proved by a walk
If it is not broken for a person, the walk harness is fixed or the finding is written down so nobody chases it again

log.note: Adversarial review of the premise first: the task's own control experiment (press a panel switch, then command+z) still had a panel press in it, so it could not tell a panel bug from a walk-wide one. Ran the missing control instead: NO panel press anywhere. /tmp/undo-nopanel.json - draw a rectangle, command+z, describe. Result: 'command+z taken by responder chain', canUndo stays true, layers stay 2, the rectangle is still there; the very next 'action undo' step takes it back (canUndo false, canRedo true, arrows empty). So command+z does the same nothing with no panel involved. The premise is wrong.

Cause was already on the record, found 2026-09-03 by a-playtest-can-check-what-command-z-really-does: macOS will not give a script-launched background app focus, so SwiftUI never re-evaluates the Commands body and the probe's menu bar is frozen at launch, every window-scoped item dimmed with a nil action. Edit > Undo is that item (EditorCommands.swift, CommandGroup replacing .undoRedo), so NSApp.mainMenu.performKeyEquivalent returns false and the press falls through to the responder chain, where nothing handles command+z. Every state block in every walk says appActive: false.

Answer to acceptance 1, as far as a runner can reach it. The panel change is undoable and the command command+z is wired to reverses it: /tmp/undo-panel-state.json shows canUndo still true after pressing the Fill switch, and 'action undo' right after puts the switch back (Fill rows back, canRedo true, the rectangle untouched, so it undid the panel change and not the draw). What no walk can ever test is the keystroke reaching that enabled item in a frontmost app, because the probe can never be frontmost. Handed to the user in queue/audits/2026-09-16-undo-after-a-panel-click.json as its first question.

Acceptance 3, the harness fix. The loud 'no action behind it, so NOTHING HAPPENED' note was wired to takenBy == menu, which is the one case where it can never fire: a dead item does not take the press. So the line read a bare 'command+z taken by responder chain' and two runners read that as the app. Now the item is named however the press was routed. Verified on a real run: 'command+z taken by responder chain (Edit > Undo carries this chord, but that item is dimmed and empty, so the MENU did not run: macOS will not give a background app focus ... use an action step.)'

Landed Scripts/playtest/panel-change-can-be-taken-back-walk.json so the finding is held rather than only written: press the Fill switch, expect it off, press command+z, expect it STILL off with the log line saying why, action undo, expect it on. Passes, 19 steps. docs/design/playtest-harness.md now says plainly that command+z after a panel click is not a bug and has been chased twice.

Caveat on the evidence: the Mac's screen was locked for this whole task (it still is), so the walks ran under PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1, the harness's own hatch for working on the harness. Everything I leaned on is EditorState model state read by describe (canUndo, canRedo, layers, colour rows) and key routing, none of which needs the window drawn, and the no-panel control matches what the two unlocked runs on 2026-09-12 reported word for word. No captures were possible, so there are none. The new walk needs a re-run on an unlocked screen before its expects count as a normal green; the next sweep does that.
